mutability_values.READ_ONLY: Viewing and non-mutating reads only. Preserve historical state.
mutability_values.REUSABLE: Use only approved actions that leave or restore known safe state. Verify after use.
mutability_values.DISPOSABLE: Provision for authorized state-changing tests and replace after use.
mutability_values.CONSUMABLE: One-time state. Mark consumed after use and select a fresh fixture.
mutability_values.UNKNOWN: Mutation prohibited until the owner clarifies safety.

health_values.READY: Suitable for its documented purpose and scope, including archived evidence.
health_values.NEEDS_VERIFICATION: Locators, suitability or current staging state need verification. A requirement remains unprovisioned.
health_values.CONSUMED: One-time or disposable state has been used.
health_values.STALE: Known state no longer matches the documented test need.
health_values.BROKEN: Fixture has a known blocking issue.
health_values.RESERVED: Reserved for a named run. Consult reserved_for before use.

kinds.FIXTURE: Known historical or current staging entity. Check its health before use.
kinds.HISTORICAL_EVIDENCE: Preserved proof of an earlier journey for read-only inspection.
kinds.REQUIREMENT: Unprepared or unbound scenario specification. Null locator means no usable staging record is established.

selection_rule: Search fixtures first for the scenario.
Use a matching READY fixture within its documented scope.
If only a matching NEEDS_VERIFICATION fixture exists, verify its current state before use.
If no suitable established fixture exists, consult requirements.
Use a requirement only after separate provisioning or binding, verification and promotion into fixtures.
Never invent a locator to satisfy a requirement.
Before use, check mutability, reservations and prior mutations. Before changing state, verify critical state and task authorization.
After the run, update health, provenance, reservations and known mutations.
metadata.fresh_fixture_rule: When a test needs a clean state and current state is uncertain, use another approved synthetic fixture or prepare a fresh disposable fixture through normal product/API setup when separately authorized. Do not manually repair production-like records to force the expected state. Apply this to RSVP, slot decisions, invitations, claims, payments, transfers and refunds.
metadata.real_data_rule: Use approved synthetic staging records for destructive acceptance. If only real customer or user data is available for the needed scenario, stop and ask the owner for authorization.
metadata.provider_rule: Provider capability establishes suitability only. Payments, SMS, email and provider configuration changes require explicit task authorization.
metadata.provenance_rule: Record the verification date and exact frontend/backend SHAs only when supported by evidence. Null means unavailable or inapplicable. A historical observation provides no assurance of current availability or sale state. Null reset_required means reset needs assessment.
metadata.links: Resolve acceptance_item_refs in ACCEPTANCE_STATE.json and finding_refs in FINDINGS.json. Source refs prefixed with acceptance: resolve in the Acceptance State sources registry. Other source refs resolve below. fixture_refs link catalog dependencies across fixtures and requirements. Count the CROSS_ROLE area as the major integration scenarios.
metadata.promotion_rule: After separate provisioning or binding and verification, promote the established record into fixtures. Keep the catalog ID where practical and preserve useful requirement or history references. Remove the superseded active requirement and keep dependency references resolvable.
